concepts.name: Feature shock, minivation, hidden gem, undead
concepts.decision: Which monetization failure could this proposal create?
concepts.applies_when: A new product is proposed before demand, configuration, and willingness to pay are established.
questions: Who would pay for which outcome?
Which observations distinguish lack of demand from the wrong configuration or price?
cautions: A rejected proposal alone does not establish any one failure pattern.

concepts.name: Early willingness-to-pay conversation
concepts.decision: What outcome will this customer pay for, and under which conditions?
concepts.applies_when: Purchase acceptance, rejection reasons, or willingness to pay remain unconfirmed.
questions: What did the customer say caused the rejection?
Which outcome has a buyer, budget, and acceptable price?
cautions: Usage, praise, and a successful pilot do not establish willingness to pay.
Do not infer that a rejected offer was too expensive without evidence.

concepts.name: Needs-based segmentation
concepts.decision: Which customers share needs and willingness to pay?
concepts.applies_when: One offer is expected to satisfy customers with different priorities.
questions: Which needs and price acceptance differ between customers?
Who is the buyer and who uses the product?
cautions: Firm size or industry alone does not establish a needs-based segment.

concepts.name: Leaders, fillers, killers and product configuration
concepts.decision: Which features belong in an offer customers will purchase?
concepts.applies_when: A proposed feature bundle includes capabilities with different customer value.
questions: Which feature drives the purchase?
Which feature is merely convenient, or deters purchase when customers must pay for it?
cautions: Feature classification must come from customer evidence, not engineering preference.

concepts.name: Unbundling and separate offers
concepts.decision: Would separating capabilities improve purchase acceptance and the business case?
concepts.applies_when: Customers already have part of a bundled solution or value only a subset.
questions: What benefit would the separate offer deliver to this customer?
Will the buyer pay for the remaining scope and its operating costs?
cautions: Removing a component does not by itself prove demand or justify a particular price.

concepts.name: Monetization model and charging metric
concepts.decision: How should customers pay for the value delivered?
concepts.applies_when: Choosing between seat, usage, subscription, or outcome-based charging.
questions: Which charging metric will customers accept?
How does the metric track customer value and operating cost?
cautions: Choosing a charging metric does not establish its price level.

concepts.name: Pricing strategy and price-setting principles
concepts.decision: Which pricing goals and response rules should guide the offer?
concepts.applies_when: A launch price or market position is being chosen.
questions: What objective should the price achieve?
Which evidence and rules govern changes to that price?
cautions: A low price is not a substitute for a demonstrated customer benefit.

concepts.name: Living business case
concepts.decision: Does measured demand support the economics of this offer?
concepts.applies_when: Revenue, adoption, price, or cost assumptions drive a build decision.
questions: Which assumptions are measured and which remain hypotheses?
Which customer evidence would change the investment decision?
cautions: Update assumptions when evidence changes; distinguish targets from observations.

concepts.name: Customer benefit statements and value communication
concepts.decision: How should the offer explain a benefit the customer recognizes?
concepts.applies_when: A technically accurate feature description does not explain the customer's outcome.
questions: What can the customer accomplish because of this capability?
Which claim can be supported by customer evidence or a measured result?
cautions: Do not present unmeasured improvements or proposed capabilities as established results.

concepts.name: Behavioral pricing experiments
concepts.decision: Which price presentation helps customers evaluate the offer?
concepts.applies_when: Testing alternative price presentations or purchase options.
questions: What observable purchase behavior would support this tactic?
Does the comparison use genuinely comparable offers?
cautions: Test a tactic rather than assuming a general behavioral effect will hold.

concepts.name: Price integrity and discount response
concepts.decision: How should the company respond to price pressure?
concepts.applies_when: A customer requests a discount or a competitor cuts price.
questions: What evidence shows that changing price will change the purchase decision?
Which response follows the agreed pricing strategy?
cautions: Do not treat a change in product scope as a like-for-like discount.

concepts.name: Cross-functional monetization pilot
concepts.decision: How should the team adopt and test the monetization process?
concepts.applies_when: Introducing customer-value and pricing decisions into product development.
questions: Which pilot can test the process?
Who owns customer evidence, product decisions, sales, and financial assumptions?
cautions: A process pilot needs measurable decisions and cross-functional ownership.
